extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and parties to USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures governing disciplinary findings, sanctions (suspension), publication, and conditions for reinstatement for practitioners registered to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 CFR § 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to practitioners registered to practice before the USPTO; grounds and procedures must be consistent with cited statutes and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO disciplinary rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration number and admission status are relevant to applicability; violations of the Code (e.g., § 10.23 provisions) form the basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for discipline — conduct reflecting adversely on fitness
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) by engaging in any conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: being suspended from practice of law on ethical grounds by a state authority (here, Illinois suspension for misuse of confidential client information and misrepresentations) can constitute such conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Proposed Settlement Agreement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.26
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Settlement Agreement sets forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions and satisfies the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid proposed settlement resolves disciplinary action and must impose discipline consistent with the regulations (e.g., reciprocal discipline per § 11.24). The Agreement must be submitted for approval to the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposed sanction — suspension period and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be suspended for one year from practice in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters before the United States Patent and Trademark Office, commencing on the date this Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension applies to all categories of practice before the Office (patent, trademark, non-patent). The effective date is the signing date of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the terms of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during the term of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 governs duties and restrictions of suspended practitioners (e.g., limitations on practice, client notice, handling of client matters). Compliance for the full period is a condition of later reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to facilitate compliance (temporary practice authorization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date the Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after the date the Final Order is signed for the sole purpose of facilitating Respondent's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrow, time-limited recognition is solely to allow the suspended practitioner to take actions necessary to wind down or transfer client matters in accordance with § 11.58(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order and shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension, grounds, and relevant facts; and, in accord with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, shall give notice of public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice should include practitioner name, registration number, basis for discipline, and reference to the settlement and statutes. Disciplinary decisions are posted at the OED Reading Room (URL provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure ("PKI") certificates relating to client matters; Respondent shall not obtain a USPTO customer number or a PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative steps are required to prevent the suspended practitioner from accessing or representing matters electronically; reinstatement is prerequisite to regaining such access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions required for reinstatement (37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c) criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must petition for reinstatement and show proof to the satisfaction of the OED Director that: (1) Respondent has the good moral character and reputation, competency, and learning in law required under 37 C.F.R. § 11.7 for admission; (2) the resumption of Respondent's practice before the Office will not be detrimental to the administration of justice or subversive to the public interest; (3) Respondent has complied with the provisions of the Final Order for the full period of suspension; and (4) Respondent has complied with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 for the full period of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is discretionary and contingent on both character/competency findings and demonstrable compliance with the suspension terms and § 11.58 obligations for the entire suspension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future use of the disciplinary record
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Proposed Settlement Agreement or this Final Order shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct brought to the attention of the Office, and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding (i) as an aggravating factor to be taken into consideration in determining any discipline to be imposed and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record may be used both offensively and defensively in future actions; prior discipline can increase sanctions or undermine future representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement can specify how costs are allocated; here, each party bears its own costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content and public posting practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Suspension includes the practitioner's name and registration number, the fact of a one-year suspension for violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5), a brief description of the misconduct (use of confidential client information and misrepresentations), and statement that the action results from a settlement under cited statutes and regulations. Disciplinary decisions are posted at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice serves to inform the public and other authorities; it follows a standard form in this Final Order (explicit phrasing shown).
